title: Sanitation workers protest in Bhopal and announce indefinite strike

tea.why: Sanitation workers are protesting for better wages, job security, and regularisation of their employment status.
tea.want: Workers demand a minimum monthly salary of Rs 25,000, regularisation of contractual staff, and an end to outsourcing.
tea.changed: Nov 4: An indefinite strike by over 23,000 sanitation workers across Madhya Pradesh is set to begin, impacting garbage collection services.

summary: Sanitation workers from across Madhya Pradesh gathered at Neelam Park in Bhopal on November 3 to protest for improved working conditions. Organised by the Akhil Bharatiya Safai Mazdoor Trade Union, the demonstration included workers from various districts. Participants are demanding regularisation of contractual roles, a minimum monthly salary of Rs 25,000, and the restoration of pension schemes. Union president Maganlal Jhanjhot stated that previous protests failed to yield results, prompting the decision to initiate an indefinite statewide strike starting November 4. In Bhopal, the impact was noted as approximately 5,000 municipal workers did not report for duty on Tuesday. While the union used municipal garbage collection vehicles to announce the protest, officials noted that such use of public equipment for union announcements is not permitted.
organizers: Akhil Bharatiya Safai Mazdoor Trade Union
demands: End to outsourcing of sanitation work
Restoration of the Old Pension Scheme
response: No official response reported in the sources.

crowd.text: Approximately 5,000 BMC sanitation workers did not report for duty on Tuesday according to Free Press Journal.

updates.text: Sanitation workers held a protest at Neelam Park in Bhopal and threatened an indefinite strike starting November 4.
An indefinite strike by over 23,000 sanitation workers across Madhya Pradesh is scheduled to commence.
